links.outcome: Accuracy and retrieval metrics of RAG with different chunking strategies
links.effect: Adaptive chunking accuracy 2.37 vs baseline 1.63 (p = 0.001); precision 0.50 vs 0.17, recall 0.88 vs 0.40, F1 0.64 vs 0.24.
links.quote: Adaptive chunking achieved the highest accuracy-87% (Likert 2.37 ± 0.72) versus baseline 50% (1.63 ± 0.72; p = 0.001)-and the highest relevance (93%, 2.90 ± 0.40).

unlisted_practices: Adaptive document chunking strategy (semantic boundaries with micro-headers) for RAG corpora to improve retrieval precision and answer accuracy

links.effect: Adaptive accuracy 87% versus baseline 50% (Likert 2.37 ± 0.72 vs 1.63 ± 0.72; p = 0.001).
links.quote: Adaptive chunking achieved the highest accuracy-87% (Likert 2.37 ± 0.72) versus baseline 50% (1.63 ± 0.72; p = 0.001)-and the highest relevance (93%, 2.90 ± 0.40).

links.effect: Basic fixed-size chunking had precision 0.17, recall 0.40, and F1 0.24.
links.quote: Conversely, the basic fixed-size chunking model performed lowest, with 0.17 (0.04–0.32) precision, 0.40 (0.10–0.70) recall, and an F1 of 0.24 (0.00–0.39), indicating that fewer than one in five retrieved passages were relevant and less than half of the relevant evidence was found.

links.effect: Basic model mean accuracy 1.63 ± 0.72; 13% fully accurate and 50% at least somewhat accurate.
links.quote: Conversely, the basic model’s mean accuracy was 1.63 ± 0.72 (95% CI 1.40–1.90), with only 13% (n = 4) of responses fully accurate and 50% (n = 15) at least somewhat accurate.
